subject: Learning Methods
title: The True Cost of Multitasking
description: A quick, practical guide to The True Cost of Multitasking.

hook.text: People who multitask feel productive. Brain scans show they are doing each task worse and taking longer overall.

buildup.text: Task switching costs 15 to 25 minutes of refocus time. Even glancing at an email resets your concentration.

discovery.text: The prefrontal cortex must reload context each time you switch. This reload is slow, effortful, and error-prone.

twist.text: Heavy multitaskers actually become worse at filtering distractions over time. The habit degrades your attention skills.

climax.text: Single-tasking is the antidote. Close all tabs. Silence notifications. Do one thing until it is done.

punchline.text: Multitasking trains your brain to be distracted.

quiz.question: What happens to heavy multitaskers over time?
options: They become more efficient at managing tasks
Their ability to filter distractions actually degrades
